title: New York's 14th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 14th Congressional District features incumbent Democrat Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez seeking a fourth term in a district covering parts of the Bronx and Queens. Ocasio-Cortez faces two Democratic primary challengers: former Wall Street executive Marty Dolan, who previously challenged her in 2022, and energy executive Felipe Garcia. The Republican nominee is Diamant Hysenaj, an entrepreneur and real estate developer running on the Republican and Conservative Party lines. The district is heavily Democratic, with Ocasio-Cortez winning 68.9% in 2024. The primary is scheduled for June 23, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026.

candidates.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
candidates.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 14th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. She serves on the House Oversight and Accountability Committee and the House Natural Resources Committee. A member of the Democratic Socialists of America, she has advocated for the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, and tuition-free public college. She won re-election in 2024 with 68.9% of the vote and has nearly $15 million cash on hand for her 2026 campaign.

candidates.name: Marty Dolan
candidates.summary: Marty Dolan is a former Wall Street insurance executive challenging Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in the 2026 Democratic primary. He previously ran against Ocasio-Cortez in the 2022 primary, winning nearly 20% of the vote, and later mounted an unsuccessful campaign for NYC Public Advocate. Dolan proposes $75,000 in home equity for NYCHA residents to buy their apartments and reimbursing young workers for taxes paid upon turning 26, up to $25,000. As of June 2026, his campaign had about $8,000 cash on hand with over $33,000 in self-loans.

candidates.name: Felipe Garcia
candidates.summary: Felipe Garcia is a Hunts Point native and former Mount Sinai executive challenging Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in the 2026 Democratic primary. An energy executive and engineer, Garcia emphasizes career pathways for young people leaving high school, particularly in high-demand fields like phlebotomy and security. He states his priority is putting the district first with someone 'born and bred in the district, with no loyalty to anyone else but the upbringing that they have.' As of June 2026, his campaign had just over $4,000 cash on hand with a self-reported budget of $100,000 of his own money.

candidates.name: Diamant Hysenaj
candidates.summary: Diamant Hysenaj is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for New York's 14th Congressional District. An entrepreneur and real estate developer, Hysenaj immigrated to the United States from Albania. He has been endorsed by NYGOP Chair Ed Cox. As of March 2026, Hysenaj had raised $288,000 in contributions with $13,000 cash on hand. He will face the Democratic primary winner in the November 3, 2026 general election.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, so confidence is capped at medium despite strong fundamentals. NY-14 is a heavily Democratic district spanning parts of the Bronx and Queens. Incumbent Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez won re-election in 2024 with 68.9% of the vote, has nearly $15 million cash on hand, and is a nationally known figure seeking a fourth term. Her two Democratic primary challengers (Marty Dolan and Felipe Garcia) have negligible campaign funds — approximately $8,000 and $4,000 respectively — compared to her war chest. The Democratic primary is three days away (June 23, 2026), and AOC is overwhelmingly favored based on resources, incumbency, name recognition, and her 2022 primary performance (~80% of the vote). The Republican general election nominee, Diamant Hysenaj, raised $288,000 but faces extreme structural disadvantages in a district that voted nearly 69% for the Democrat in the last presidential-aligned cycle. A Democratic hold is virtually certain regardless of which Democrat emerges from the primary.
